_comment: Table Health Advisor settings. orphan_min_age_minutes is test scale (3, the hot window); production should be days (Iceberg's remove_orphan_files default is 3 days = 4320) so in-flight writes are never counted. orphan_scan_every_hours / retained_bytes_every_hours: 0 = whenever the table changed (test); production ~24. advisor_mode: auto | approve-only | off, the default; a table's own advisor.mode property wins. 'defaults' apply to every table; 'tables' overrides per table ('thresholds' merges key by key). Test scale: target file size is 8 MB (64x below Iceberg's 512 MB default) so small test tables show real symptoms. Thresholds were calibrated on the first gl-metrics run of S0-S6 (2026-10-02); production values are noted in the README.

compaction._comment: Tier rule (plan item 12, family incremental.tiering). Fragment: a data file under target_file_bytes / fragment_ratio; undersized segment: from there up to small_file_ratio x target. Per partition not held by a conflict: cold (no writer commit for cold_hours) -> one major pass (fragments and undersized segments into right-sized files); warm -> a minor pass over the fragments only once there are minor_min_fragments of them or the oldest has waited minor_max_wait_hours (and there are at least 2); else wait (SMALL_FILES defer). A table's advisor.compact.cold-hours / advisor.compact.minor-max-wait-hours win for the two times. Tiered passes run with partial progress (rewrite.tier_partial_progress_max_commits) and rewrite-job-order bytes-desc. TEST SCALE times 0.1 h; production 6 h cold, 8 h minor wait (agreed 2026-10-09).

cost._comment: Step 10 of a plan run (plan.py savings_estimate): fewer files means fewer GET requests for every full read of a table. ASSUMPTIONS to set per environment: full_reads_per_day (how often the table is read in full; per table under tables.<name>.cost), get_usd_per_1000 (S3 Standard GET price, us-east-1), storage_usd_per_gb_month (S3 Standard storage, us-east-1, first tier; RETAINED_STORAGE prices the bytes old snapshots keep with it: they cost storage only, since queries read the current snapshot's files). Storage comes back after expiry and the file grace and is reported as files freed until freed-file sizes are recorded.

expiry._comment: GL2.6e expiry by policy (expiry.py). Category: streaming when the table had >= streaming_min_commits_24h writer commits in the last 24 h. The table's history.expire.* properties win, then advisor.expire.max-age-hours / advisor.expire.min-snapshots, then these. max_snapshots (D3, agreed 2026-10-09: 500-1,000; 500 ~ 30 min of a 1,000-commit-an-hour writer, ~0.5 MB of metadata.json): more snapshots inside the window shorten it (each is a metadata.json entry every commit rewrites); never below the policy's min_snapshots; per table advisor.expire.max-snapshots. retained_what_if_hours: the shorter windows RETAINED_STORAGE advice prices (what old snapshots would still keep right after an expiry to each), only those shorter than the table's policy; retained_what_if_keep: the lower minimums it prices (at the policy's age), since the minimum kept holds snapshots whatever their age. There is no window floor: the advisor expires only after the ledger has caught up in the same run, with the cutoff capped at the newest snapshot it ingested (plan.py --apply, run order D1). Expiry of user tables deletes no files (freed_files.py): the files it frees wait out the file grace, then the plan deletes them. file grace: advisor.expire.file-grace-hours, else advisor.expire.reader-timeout-hours + clock_margin_minutes, else file_grace_hours, floored at file_grace_floor_hours unless from a declared timeout; TEST SCALE 0.1 h / 0.05 h / 1 min, production 12 h / 1 h / 10 min. stale_ref_hours: a tag or branch other than main older than this with no retention of its own is STALE_REF; TEST SCALE 1 h, production ~720 (30 days). retained_bytes (sibling key): full = today's all_files query (rationed by retained_bytes_every_hours) with the summary formula computed and compared; ledger (on since GL2.6f, after 27/27 tables agreed on the cluster) = the summary formula for data bytes, the old-manifest query on retained_bytes_every_hours, and the full all_files query only as the rationed fallback for a table whose formula is unknown (refs other than main, branched history, no size summaries) or not yet computed; off = not measured.

thresholds._writer_comment: GL2.7a, test scale: SNAPSHOT_RATE over 24 writer commits a day (production 288, every 5 min) that each write under snapshot_rate_small_share of a target file; the suggested trigger fills snapshot_rate_fill_share of a target file, capped at snapshot_rate_max_interval_minutes. HISTORY_LOST after history_lost_min_gaps ledger gaps within history_lost_window_days.
thresholds._unpartitioned_comment: Item 12, family tiering: a large unpartitioned table (data_bytes >= unpartitioned_min_target_files x target) with continuous appends (>= unpartitioned_appends_min_commits_24h writer commits in 24 h) is never cold: the tier rule gives it minors or waits only, no whole-table major. UNPARTITIONED_APPENDS (approval) when one of its sort, filter or time columns (advisor.time-column) has an average overlap depth (files one value falls into, from the files' bounds) of at least unpartitioned_overlap_depth: partition by time and sort within. TEST SCALE 12 commits a day; production 48 (expiry's streaming category).
thresholds._holds_comment: Item 13. The conflict hold counts only commits that can make a rewrite fail: data or delete files removed, or position deletes / deletion vectors added (equality deletes never, nor the position deletes a Flink-style upsert writes next to them). advisor.compact.blackout (table property: comma-separated UTC ranges 'HH:MM-HH:MM' or 'Sun HH:MM-HH:MM', may cross midnight) holds every partition while a run is inside it. advisor.mutable-days: a time partition that ended less than that many days ago gets no major (merges may still rewrite it); minors as usual. Hold limit: a partition the conflict hold held at every run for hold_limit_hours (time partitions: counted only from their end + the late-arrival allowance: advisor.mutable-days, else the learned lateness p99, else hold_busy_default_hours) is listed in HOLD_STARVED (approval: APPROVE=HOLD_STARVED compacts them once) or, with hold_limit_action auto, compacted anyway. A declared blackout is never overridden. TEST SCALE limit 0.2 h; production 24 h.

rewrite._comment: Options plan.py puts on the CALLs. min_input_files null = min_excess_files + 1, so every flagged partition is one the rewrite will change.

incremental._comment: GL2.5m incremental scan. Per family: off | shadow (full path decides, both compared in glue.ops.incremental_check) | on (ledger decides; spot_check_share of tables and any table not compared for reconcile_every_days are still compared). Family 1 (snapshot_ledger) passed shadow 2026-10-03 and is on; family 2 (partition_activity) reports and compares only (shadow); family 3 (learned_windows: hot window = 2 x p95 commit gap between hot_partition_minutes and hot_cap_minutes, needing min_gaps commit gaps after leaving out idle gaps longer than idle_gap_factor x the median gap; LATE_ARRIVALS' lateness trigger needs min_batches batches) shows what would change (shadow) or decides (on); the settle window it also learned was retired 2026-10-10. The only hold (holds.py, no family switch since 2026-10-10): a writer commit that removed or rewrote files in the partition within hot_partition_minutes (HOT_PARTITION, defer); appends never hold a partition. A partition writers rewrote at least thresholds.churn_partition_rate x its bytes in the last churn_window_h keeps its SMALL_FILES auto with churn advice to the owner (a note, not a hold). The still-filling hold, the per-partition and table-wide churn holds, the settle window and SETTLING were retired 2026-10-10 (the tier rule replaces them, plan item 12). A table's optional time_column lets the plan compact an appended-to unpartitioned table's older rows only. Family new_findings (GL2.6c; on since 2026-10-04 after s20 and s12 in shadow): DELETE_FILE_SPRAWL (>= thresholds.delete_sprawl_min_files position delete files in a partition whose delete ratio is under DELETE_BUILDUP's: merge them, auto), RETAINED_STORAGE (bytes only old snapshots reference at least retained_storage_min_bytes and MORE than retained_storage_min_share of the live bytes; 1.0 = more than one extra copy, since one compaction always leaves one copy for the retention window: approval) and METADATA_BLOAT (metadata.json over metadata_max_json_bytes or manifests only old snapshots reference over metadata_max_retained_bytes: approval); the byte limits are test scale, 1/64 of the production placeholders (1 GiB, 8 MiB, 1 GiB). RETAINED_STORAGE carries usd_per_month (cost.storage_usd_per_gb_month) and, with thresholds.retained_storage_min_usd_month > 0, fires only at or above that many USD a month (0 here: test-scale bytes cost fractions of a cent; production placeholder 5). shadow reports what would be added, on adds them. Family expiry_policy (GL2.6e, expiry.py): SNAPSHOT_BUILDUP when the retention policy (defaults.expiry, or the table's history.expire.* properties) would expire at least thresholds.expire_min_snapshots snapshots, instead of the snapshot count / age thresholds; STALE_REF for old tags and branches; the plan expires to the policy. shadow reports what would change; on since GL2.6f (2026-10-05) after s21, s3 and s4 in shadow. Family 4 comes later. Lookback: histogram_days, extended whole days at a time (adaptive_lookback) up to lookback_max_days until a table has min_batches / min_gaps samples. Until a table has min_batches batches, a large append later than cold_start_backfill_hours is labelled possible_backfill.
incremental._store_comment: Step 1 state store (state_store.py). store_preload_days: commits and partition activity are read in bulk this far back (default: max(histogram_days, 30) + 1); a table whose retained snapshots go further back is read again on its own. store_preload_max_rows: a kind with more rows than this in the window is not read in bulk; tables then load one by one. partition_state_keep_days: a partition no longer in the table, with no write or compaction for this long, is dropped from partition_state. retention_days also applies to partition_activity.
incremental._previous_comment: previous_scan_window_hours: the last scan's row per table (carried values, probe clocks, reuse) and recent actions are read from the logs only this far back, so the read does not grow with history; a table not scanned within it is measured in full.

ops_maintenance._comment: Upkeep of the advisor's own glue.ops tables (ops_maintenance.py), in the housekeeping pass only (one run at a time). Checks from metadata; acts only past a threshold: rewrite_data_files when it would remove >= min_excess_files files (partitions with >= min_input_files), rewrite_manifests above max_manifests, expire_snapshots when >= min_expire snapshots are older than safe_age_hours beyond the newest retain_last (safe_age_hours longer than any run, so readers in other runs keep their files), and the write.metadata.* properties. No orphan-file removal (other runs' uncommitted files look like orphans). Log: glue.ops.ops_maintenance, log_keep_days.

state._comment: Where the advisor keeps what the next run needs: postgres (the postgres block, the default) or iceberg (tables in glue.ops). Keep one backend per environment: each store only knows the runs made against it (freed files waiting for deletion, ledger watermarks, action history), so switch only by copying (make gl-pg-migrate). GL_STATE_BACKEND overrides it for one run (make ... STATE_BACKEND=iceberg). Claims stay in DynamoDB either way.

logs._comment: Where the advisor's history goes (table_metrics, symptoms, actions, ...): postgres (the default) or iceberg (glue.ops). GL_LOGS_BACKEND overrides it for one run.

postgres._comment: Used when a backend is postgres. mode driver: pg8000 over TCP (homelab pod from make gl-pg-up, or Aurora from EKS); the password comes from the env var named in password_env (the advisor-pg Secret on the homelab). mode data_api: the RDS Data API (Aurora Serverless v2 from Glue; set resource_arn and secret_arn). GL_PG_HOST / GL_PG_PORT / GL_PG_DATABASE / GL_PG_USER / GL_PG_SCHEMA / GL_PG_MODE / GL_PG_RESOURCE_ARN / GL_PG_SECRET_ARN override these.
